pairs.why: Both cacti are rendered almost the same, but A's softer light and grounded cast shadow sit a little closer to the softly shaded real duck and taxi than B's flatter, more saturated version.
This is q008 with the sides swapped: B has the softer light and grounded shadow, while A is slightly flatter and more saturated.
A's stitched leather and felt pad make it a built object like the preferred lesson saddles, while B's smooth glossy finish reads as a plastic toy or statue.
This is q010 with the sides swapped: B has the stitched leather that reads as a real object, while A looks glossy and moulded like plastic.
The ropes are nearly the same, but A's bright, saturated green background and warm sand match the vivid real cards better than B's muted green and pale sand.
This is q012 with the sides swapped: B has the vivid saturated background and warm sand that match the real cards.
A has moderate painted wood grain and a lived-in setting like the real dock and gate cards, while B's plain brown walls and empty ground look slightly too smooth and toy-like.
This is q014 with the sides swapped: B has the moderate wood detail and furnished setting, while A is a little too flat and empty.
